name: Blend and deliver bulk cement
summary: Before a rig can cement casing, the district bulk plant must blend dry oilwell cement with the additives the lab specified, in the right proportions for that well, and haul it to the lease in pneumatic bulk trucks. Bulk plant operators check the blend sheet against the approved lab design, weigh and blend the batches, take a sample for the lab and load the trucks; Class 1 drivers then haul the blend, often 150 to 300 km on lease roads, and blow it into field silos or feed the pumper during the job. The work is slow and error-prone because rigs keep moving the casing point, so blends wait in bins or trucks wait on location, a weighing or additive error only shows up if the lab tests the blend or the job goes wrong, and winter roads, storms and spring road bans add delays.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian pressure pumping company running about 16 cementing units from Alberta and northeast BC district bases with bulk blending plants, plus a Calgary cement and fluids laboratory and engineering office.
baseline.notes: Common practice of large WCSB cementing service lines in 2019-2022: dispatch board and phone, ERP inventory, tablet field tickets, lab database and spreadsheets, cement placement software; no automated blending recipe download or live job data streaming to the office as standard.

unit_of_work: one cement blend and its delivery to the wellsite
trigger: Dispatch books a cement job on the dispatch board and sends the bulk plant a blend request with the approved slurry design from the lab.
end_state: The blend has been offloaded at the wellsite and the delivery and driver logs are closed, or the job was cancelled and the held blend reused or scrapped.

volume.seasonality: Follows the drilling rig count: highest January to mid-March, lowest in April and May during spring break-up road bans, recovering through summer and autumn.

evidence.note: Kept the organisation file's volume of one blend per cement job (about 400 a month). Cementing activity tracks the rig count (src3). A few small plug and squeeze jobs use bagged cement, which this estimate ignores.

surge.cause: Winter drilling and completion peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Cementing activity tracks the rig count (src3), which peaks in the first quarter; duration and multiplier follow the organisation file's estimate.

About 5.5 hands-on hours a blend (two operators blend together) over 400 blends a month gives about 17 FTE at 130 productive hours; the plant crews of 15 also maintain the plants and silos, so blending is stated as most of their time; estimate.

About 19 driver-hours a delivery (two trucks, loading, driving both ways, offloading) over 400 deliveries; most of the 60 drivers' time; waiting at the lease is logged off duty and not counted; estimate.
Blend requests and truck assignment, about 30 minutes a job; dispatcher is an organisation file role not listed for this process; estimate.
Blend confirmation tests on about half the blends, about 75 hands-on minutes each; not listed for this process in the organisation file; estimate.
Decides what happens to blends held after a cancelled job; estimate.

systems.name: Dispatch and crew scheduling board (scheduling module, whiteboards, spreadsheets)
Laboratory test records (lab database and spreadsheets)
ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
Vehicle telematics and electronic driver logs
Electronic field ticketing on tablets, linked to the ERP price book
HSE incident, hazard assessment and audit system

steps.name: Enter job and send blend request
steps.description: The dispatcher enters the cement job on the dispatch board with the rig, lease location, casing string and expected call time, and emails or phones the district bulk plant a blend request with the tonnage and the lab's slurry design number.

error.defect_description: Wrong tonnage or design number copied from the call sheet

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Check blend sheet against approved design
steps.description: The bulk plant operator opens the lab record for the design, compares the cement class, additive names and percentages by weight of cement, and the tonnage with the request, and checks the lab has marked the design approved for this well.

error.defect_description: Additive percentage misread from the design

next.condition: design not yet approved or does not match

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Chase lab for approved design
steps.description: The operator phones or emails the lab and the cement engineer to ask for the approved design or a corrected blend sheet, because the pilot tests are still running or the request named an old revision.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Check silo and additive stock
steps.description: The operator checks the silo level gauges for the cement class and counts the additive bags or totes on the floor, compares them with the batch needs and the inventory figure in the ERP, and notes anything short.

error.defect_description: Silo level over-read, so the blend runs short of cement

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Request cement or additive replenishment
steps.description: The operator emails supply chain a replenishment request for the short cement class or additive with the quantity and the job date, and asks whether a pneumatic trailer can come before the job.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait for cement or additive delivery
steps.description: The cement supplier's pneumatic trailer or the additive shipment arrives at the plant and is blown into the silo or stacked in the warehouse, which takes from a few hours for a district transfer to two days from the supplier.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Calculate batch weights and print blend ticket
steps.description: The operator converts the design's additive percentages by weight of cement into kilograms per batch for the plant's weigh tank size and the number of batches, writes them on the blend ticket and records the batch plan in the blend log spreadsheet.

error.defect_description: Arithmetic or unit error in additive weight per batch

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Hold pre-shift hazard assessment and plant checks
steps.description: The two plant operators complete a field level hazard assessment for blending (silica dust, confined bins, air pressure, moving conveyors), check compressor, dust collector and scale readings, and put on respirators before opening the bins.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 2 sections 7-8 (hazard assessment with worker participation) and Part 4 silica provisions; company bulk plant lockout and confined space procedures

evidence.note: Hazard assessment and silica provisions from the OHS Code table of contents (src8); times are estimates.

steps.name: Weigh and blend batches
steps.description: The operators weigh cement into the weigh tank, add the dry additives by hand or from additive bins, and air-blend each batch by transferring it between tanks two or three times until it is uniform, repeating until the full tonnage is in the storage bin.

error.defect_description: Additive left out of a batch or poor mixing leaves layers of different composition

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Take blend sample from conveying line
steps.description: During the last transfer the operator cuts samples from the conveying line into a labelled pail, records the blend ticket number, and keeps a retained sample at the plant; for intermediate, production and critical jobs a sample goes to the lab.

error.defect_description: Sample taken from the top of the bin is not representative

next.condition: blend sample goes to the lab

evidence.note: Bulk-blend samples are taken from the conveying line during blending and mixed in the lab with the actual mixing water (src4); share sent to the lab is an estimate.

steps.name: Courier blend sample to the lab
steps.description: The sample travels to the cement laboratory with a hot-shot driver, a crew truck heading that way or the next courier run, together with a jug of the rig's mix water when the lab does not already have it.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Run blend confirmation test
steps.description: A laboratory technologist mixes the field blend with the rig water, runs thickening time in the consistometer at the well's test schedule and a fluid loss test, and compares the results with the pilot results for the same design before entering them in the lab database.

control.basis: Company cementing quality standard: field blend tested against pilot design for intermediate and production casing

next.condition: thickening time or fluid loss off

evidence.note: Blend samples mixed with the actual mix water (src4); thickening time and fluid loss test methods (src5). Failure share is an estimate.

steps.name: Recommend blend correction
steps.description: The technologist works out how much retarder or other additive to add to the bin to bring thickening time back into the design window, checks it with a quick lab mix, and phones the correction to the bulk plant.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Re-blend or add additive
steps.description: The plant operators add the corrective additive to the blend and transfer it again until uniform, or dump and re-blend when the error cannot be corrected, then record the change on the blend ticket.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Assign bulk trucks and drivers
steps.description: The dispatcher picks the bulk trucks and drivers for the job from the dispatch board, checking drivers' hours under the oil well service vehicle permit and truck availability, and tells the plant when the trucks will load.

error.defect_description: Driver assigned without enough hours left in the cycle

evidence.note: Oil well service vehicle permit rules on off-duty periods (src7); times are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for rig call time
steps.description: The blend stays in the bin until the rig is close to landing casing; rigs move the call time when drilling or running casing goes faster or slower, and sometimes cancel or defer the job.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Inspect and load bulk trucks
steps.description: Each driver completes the pre-trip inspection, spots the truck under the plant's loading spout, loads the blend and weighs the truck on the scale, then seals the hatches and checks the air system.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Record load and update inventory
steps.description: The plant operator records each truck's scale weight against the blend ticket, writes the bill of lading and load ticket, and books the cement and additives used out of plant inventory in the ERP.

error.defect_description: Additive usage keyed wrongly, so inventory and the field ticket disagree

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Haul blend to the wellsite
steps.description: The drivers haul the loaded trucks from the district base to the lease, usually two to four hours on highways and lease roads, slowed by winter conditions, storms and spring road-ban weight limits.

evidence.note: Road bans lower allowed weights during thaw (src9); distances and times are estimates.

steps.name: Wait on location for the cement crew
steps.description: The trucks wait on the lease until the rig has finished running and circulating casing and the cementing crew is ready; drivers log the waiting time as off duty when they do no work.

evidence.note: Waiting time at a well site may be logged off duty (src7); durations are estimates.

steps.name: Rig in and offload blend
steps.description: The drivers rig in hoses, blow the blend into field silos or feed the cementing unit's mixing system directly during the job, keeping air pressure and rate steady so the pumper holds slurry density, then rig out.

error.defect_description: Air supply interrupted during the job, causing a density swing

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Haul leftover blend back to the plant
steps.description: When excess cement remains, a driver hauls it back to the base and blows it into the plant's reclaim bin, labelled with the blend ticket so the plant can decide whether to reuse it.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Decide use of held blend
steps.description: The cementing supervisor for the district decides whether the blend held for a cancelled or deferred job can be kept for the rescheduled job, blended into another design after a lab check, or must be scrapped, and tells the plant.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Drive back to base
steps.description: The drivers drive the empty trucks back to the district base, fuel them and park them in the yard, reporting any defect found on the trip.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Close delivery ticket and driver log
steps.description: Each driver completes the electronic log with driving, on-duty and waiting time, attaches the signed delivery ticket and scale ticket, and hands any paper copies to the district office for the field ticket.

error.defect_description: Delivery ticket missing or unsigned, delaying the customer field ticket

evidence.note: Driver logs under the oil well service vehicle permit (src7); times are estimates.

exceptions.name: Lab design not yet approved
exceptions.description: The pilot tests are still running or the request named an old design revision, so the plant waits before blending.

exceptions.name: Stock short
exceptions.description: A cement class or additive is short and must be replenished before blending.

exceptions.name: Blend fails confirmation test
exceptions.description: The field blend's thickening time or fluid loss does not match the pilot, and the plant corrects or re-blends it.

exceptions.name: Job cancelled or deferred
exceptions.description: The rig cancels or defers the cement job after the blend is made.

exceptions.name: Leftover blend
exceptions.description: Excess cement is hauled back to the plant's reclaim bin.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from blend request to delivery record closed

evidence.note: Estimate: blends are usually made the day before the job, and trucks roll a few hours before the rig lands casing; long tails come from rigs moving the call time and from blend retests.

benchmarks.population: Surface, intermediate and production casing jobs

evidence.note: Estimate from typical slurry tonnages of 10 to 80 tonnes and truck capacities of about 25 to 30 tonnes.

pain_points.description: Rigs move the casing call time by hours or days, so blends sit in bins and trucks and drivers wait on the lease.

evidence.note: Waiting time at well sites is common enough that hours-of-service rules address it (src7); size estimated.

pain_points.description: A weighing or additive error in the blend is only caught when the blend is lab tested; untested blends carry the error to the job.

evidence.note: Lab and field results differ and blend samples are needed to check them (src4).

pain_points.description: Blend sheets are re-keyed from the lab design into the plant's batch calculation and again into the ERP and field ticket.

evidence.note: Typical practice of the period: no recipe download from the lab database to the plant controls.

pain_points.description: Winter road conditions, storms and spring road bans slow or stop heavy bulk trucks.

evidence.note: Road bans during thaw (src9).

sources.title: Management's Discussion and Analysis for the year ended December 31, 2022
sources.supports: Cementing activity tracks the WCSB rig count (201 rigs in Q4 2022, 176 in Q4 2021); 17 cementing units operated in Q4 2022; annual average of 16 cementing units in the field in 2021 and 2022; cementing about 16-19% of revenue; 1,335,000 tonnes of proppant pumped in 2022 and 1,364,000 in 2021; oilfield cement and proppant sourced from suppliers in Canada and the United States.

sources.title: Shear rate has greater influence on cement slurry properties than total mixing energy
sources.publisher: Oil & Gas Journal (Paul Padgett, Halliburton Energy Services)
sources.supports: Bulk-blend samples taken from the conveying line during blending and mixed in the lab with the actual mixing water under the API procedure; field mixing equipment runs at lower shear than lab blenders, so field slurry properties (free water especially) often differ from lab values; thickening time and fluid loss changed only slightly with mixing energy.

sources.title: Oil Well Cement Testing Simple Guide
sources.supports: Thickening time in an HPHT consistometer (70 Bc end point, some operators 50 Bc); crush tests on moulded cubes after 8, 16 or 24 hours; ultrasonic cement analyser runs usually about 24 hours; fluid loss collected for 30 minutes at circulating temperature; free water test stands about two hours; rheology on a Fann viscometer for displacement and ECD modelling.

sources.title: Commercial Vehicle Drivers Hours of Service Regulations (SOR/2005-313), section 63, version in force 2019-06-12 to 2021-06-11
sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: Oil well service vehicle permits: three 24-hour off-duty periods in any 24 days instead of the regular cycle; waiting or standby time at a well site may be logged off duty if no work is done; drivers need oil and gas field safety training.

sources.title: Occupational Health and Safety Code (table of contents)
sources.supports: Part 2 Hazard Assessment, Elimination and Control: section 7 hazard assessment, section 8 worker participation, section 9 hazard elimination and control; Part 4 harmful substances including section 28 general provisions for asbestos, silica, coal dust and lead and section 40 health assessments for silica exposure; Part 18 respiratory protective equipment.

sources.title: Road bans
sources.supports: Road bans lower maximum weights when roads are weak or thawing; spring heavy-haul period starts when thaw depth reaches 25 cm, post-thaw from about June 16; exemptions by permit through the Central Permit Office; local bans set by counties and municipal districts.

assumptions: Loaded hourly costs and headcounts are taken from the organisation file (wage x 1.35).
One blend per cement job; two bulk trucks on an ordinary job, shown with people = 2 on the driving and offloading steps.
The blend is sampled for the lab on about 55% of jobs (intermediate, production and critical casing); surface casing blends usually keep only a retained sample.
Dispatcher and laboratory technologist take part in this process but are not listed among the process_map roles in the organisation file.

The process_map entry sends a shipment request to dangerous goods shipping on every job; in practice dry cement is not a regulated dangerous good and only some liquid additives sent with the crew need TDG paperwork, so the link is kept but is occasional.
Load tickets go to field ticket preparation; this link is not in the organisation file.

The lab facility in the organisation file is one resource per laboratory, which a single test does not tie up; the blend test holds one consistometer instead, a resource the organisation file lacks (count of 10 across the company labs is an estimate).

occupied_min on the truck steps is per truck; with two trucks a job, truck-hours are about twice the simulated figure, roughly 9,000 truck-hours a month at 400 jobs against the organisation file's 45 trucks at a mode of 190 available hours (8,550), so the truck fleet is fully used at mode volume.
Bulk truck hours are counted in this process, not in the cement job process, to avoid double counting.
